name: Pidilite Industries Ltd
title: Pidilite Industries Ltd - 500331 - Transcript Of Earnings Call

read.thesis: Q2 standalone UVG 10.7% and H1 UVG 11% held, but EBITDA margin fell to 20.4% on VAM at ~$1,630 avg; management reaffirms 20–24% corridor, upper end for H2 after 12–15% price hikes and October round.

triggers.label: H2 margin toward higher end of 20–24%

summary.headline: Pidilite Q2 FY27 standalone revenue grew 21.7% on 10.7% UVG, but EBITDA margin fell 430 bps to 20.4% as VAM input costs spiked.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue was just under INR4,000 crore in Q2 FY27, up 21.7% in nominal terms, with underlying volume growth (UVG) of 10.7% that management called broad-based. Gross margin fell 720 bps YoY and sequentially as VAM consumption rate hit $1,630/t versus $1,370 in Q1, and EBITDA margin came in at the low end of the range at 20.4%. H1 standalone revenue grew 22% with UVG of 11% and H1 EBITDA margin of 23.5%. Management priced up 12-15% in Q1, cut back on pricing in Q2 as VAM cooled, then took another round from October 1 and flagged a possible further 3-5% round.

financial_highlights.change: Down 430 bps YoY; lower end of 20-24% corridor
EBITDA up 53%; Dubai, Bangladesh, Kenya, Thailand each grew >20%
Consumer & Bazaar +22%, B2B +22%; Nina the only headwind (waterproofing workfront shortage)
Benefited from low-cost inventory from Q4 FY26

segments.name: Consumer & Bazaar (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 11.1% in Q2 and 11.6% in H1; Roff, Dr. Fixit and new campaigns in Q3; Stainoff getting strong quick-commerce response.

segments.name: B2B (standalone)
segments.commentary: UVG of 9.2% in Q2 and 8.3% in H1; projects business reorganised into segment-based approach (builders, hotels/hospitals/education, EPC) with momentum expected into Q3.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue +21.8% and EBITDA +53% in Q2; four markets each grew above 20%.

segments.name: Domestic subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Revenue +22.2% in Q2, led by ICA (wood finish) and construction chemical JVs; Nina down on monsoon-period workfront constraints.

guidance_outlook: H2 EBITDA margin expected within the 20-24% corridor, ideally the upper end, based on VAM around $1,200/t and the October pricing.
Management aims to keep UVG in double digits and ultimately move to early teens over time; not chasing volume for its own sake.
Further price increase of 3-5% in areas of heightened inflation may follow towards end of Q3 or early Q4, depending on the environment.
Margin base view remains 20-24%, with a bias to the higher end and gradual inching up.
capex_capacity: Exterior render (Grupopuma JV) production currently at Rajasthan facility; management evaluating additional plants given momentum.
Newly launched Araldite Wud, Araldite Stone X and Wud-X are new products addressing premium wood and stone segments.
Fevicol Multi Lock and X-Per piloted products going national in November 2026.
No Pidilite VAM capacity; management says a competitor's new VAM plant is sub-scale and offers no cost advantage to Pidilite.
demand_pricing: Price increase of 12-15% taken in Q1 FY27 across high-inflation categories, in two staggered phases; further round taken October 1 on Fevicol and Dr. Fixit.
Management says entire absolute cost increase has been passed on, but percentage margin recovery lags; calibrated pricing going forward.
VAM was $800-900/t through FY26, spiked to about $2,000 after West Asia conflict, cooled to around $900-1,000 in Q2, and was about $1,200 at the time of the call.
Urban growth picked up and urban slightly ahead of rural in Q2 for the first time in a long time; rural growth stable.
Competitive intensity described as reasonable and unchanged; local competitors in Fevicol and Dr. Fixit are a mix of very local and large players.
Exports into West Asia still underperforming due to shipping disruption.
Fevicol delivered 50-100 bps better growth than in the past.

qa_highlights.question: Was pricing delayed in expectation of geopolitical resolution, and what is current VAM and crude pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut back pricing in Q2 as VAM cooled to around $900-1,000, then took a round on October 1 as VAM rose again; current VAM about $1,200 and crude about $115. Q3 and H2 margins expected in the 20-24% corridor, ideally the upper end.

qa_highlights.question: Are local players exiting as in detergents, and what share of raw materials is crude-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: No fundamental shift in competitive intensity; competitors in Dr. Fixit and tile adhesives are large companies. Sandeep said bulk of raw and packaging materials are crude-linked, but pass-through lags due to demand-supply dynamics.

qa_highlights.question: Are Araldite Wud and Araldite White new products and how are they priced?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, they are new to the portfolio and aimed at the premium wood and stone segments; management also cited Wonderproof, M-Seal Advance and Fevicol Multi Lock/X-Per as fundamental innovations.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken and how sustainable is volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Round one was 12-15% in high-inflation areas; a further 3-5% round is planned in some areas. Management said demand has been robust, targets double-digit UVG with a GDP-linked assumption of 6.5-7% real growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company seeing productivity gains from AI and operating leverage on A&P and staff costs?
qa_highlights.answer: AI is being used for marketing content, influencer work, analytics and supply chain/manufacturing variance reduction; productivity gains are a later phase and headcount reduction is not the aim during growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk from a competitor's new VAM plant, and is backward integration planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no cost advantage in domestic VAM given scale economics and India's lack of ethylene/acetic acid advantage, and prefers procurement plus cycle management.

qa_highlights.question: Has demand held up despite macro headwinds and job-loss concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says demand in India has held up and the team is not assuming macro improvement for the rest of the year; exports to West Asia remain weak.

risks_watch: Volatility in VAM and crude: VAM at about $1,200/t versus $1,370 in Q1 and $1,630 in Q2; further spikes would pressure H2 margins.
Pass-through lag: management says percentage margin recovery needs more than 2x cost increase at a 50% gross margin level, so margin repair is gradual.
Further price increase of 3-5% could affect volume momentum in a period of elevated inflation.
West Asia conflict, shipping disruption and El Nino effects not fully baked into the outlook; exports to West Asia underperforming.
Nina waterproofing headwind in monsoon period; Q3 retail and projects momentum to be verified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and H2 margin recovery to the upper end of the 20-24% corridor, but cautious on near-term input cost volatility, with management repeatedly asking investors to judge margins on a half-yearly or longer-term basis.
key_quotes: We will manage it for the year. We will manage demand as well.

we remain very confident of Q3 and quite confident of the full second half that we should be able to deliver in our EBITDA margin corridor of 20% to 24%, ideally in the slightly higher end of the corridor.
So the second quarter saw the full impact of elevated input costs.
for us, staff cost is not an objective by itself.

adds.what: Exterior render (Grupopuma JV) production currently at Rajasthan facility; additional plants under evaluation

growth.why: H1 standalone revenue grew 22% with UVG of 11% and Q2 revenue up 21.7%, backed by price increases, volume growth and new launches (Araldite Wud, Stone X, Fevicol Multi Lock going national Nov 2026), but no specific capacity additions were quantified and margin guidance is a 20-24% corridor rather than a growth target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides H2 EBITDA margin within the 20-24% corridor, ideally upper end, with VAM around $1,200/t and October pricing; H1 margin was 23.5% but Q2 fell to 20.4% on VAM at $1,630/t, so recovery is guided but gradual.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exterior render (Grupopuma JV) is produced at the Rajasthan facility and management is evaluating additional plants given momentum, but no capacity additions were quantified or dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: UVG was 10.7% in Q2 and 11% in H1 (Consumer & Bazaar 11.1%, B2B 9.2%), and management aims to stay in double digits, aspiring to early teens over time, though a further 3-5% price round may weigh on volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and the only capacity signal is evaluation of additional exterior render plants given momentum, with no board approval or land mentioned.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin view is held at 20-24% with bias to the upper end, and management is not assuming macro improvement, so no upgrade signalled beyond the corridor.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell to 20.4% (down 430 bps YoY) on VAM at $1,630/t, and crude near $115 plus West Asia shipping disruption could pressure H2 margins if VAM spikes again.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fevicol Multi Lock and X-Per go national in November 2026, and Araldite Wud, Araldite Stone X and Wud-X are already launched for premium wood and stone segments.

rows.label: Further 3-5% price round
rows.when: end Q3 or early Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management flagged a possible 3-5% increase in high-inflation areas after 12-15% taken in Q1 and another round from October 1, depending on the environment.

rows.label: International subsidiaries momentum
rows.why: International revenue grew 21.8% and EBITDA 53% in Q2, with Dubai, Bangladesh, Kenya and Thailand each above 20%, though West Asia exports remain weak on shipping disruption.

rows.label: Projects B2B reorganisation into segments
rows.why: B2B UVG was 9.2% in Q2 and 8.3% in H1, and the segment-based reorganisation (builders, hotels/hospitals/education, EPC) is expected to build momentum into Q3, which still needs verification.

tone.note: Management was confident on double-digit demand and H2 margin recovery to the upper end of the 20-24% corridor, but cautious on VAM and crude volatility and asked investors to judge margins over half-year or longer; analysts probed pricing timing, competitor VAM plant risk and backward integration.
